source.data_source: Schefer et al. (Sandia) propane-air variable-density turbulent jet experiment. Centerline U from LDV (paxv.jet.txt); centerline Y_C3H8 from Rayleigh mixture-fraction (paxray.txt); radial U at x/D=30 from LDV (p30v.jet.txt). Files distributed via the TNF Workshop archive and bundled in the SU2 V&V repo at rans/SANDIA_jet/Postprocessing/SANDC3H8.JET/.
source.cross_code_check: SU2 INC_RANS-SST V2003m and OpenFOAM rhoReactingFoam reproduce the experimental centerline U/Y_C3H8 decay within ~10% in the SU2 V&V plots; both solvers' sampled fields are stored alongside the experiment under data1994/, data2003/, dataOpenFOAM/.
source.experiment_citation: R. W. Schefer et al., 'Propane Jet Data', Sandia National Laboratories, TNF Workshop archive (1994 LDV + 2003 reanalysis). Bulk jet velocity 53 m/s, jet diameter D=5.26 mm, Re_D=68168.

mesh_cell_count.description: Total cell count of the agent's 2-D axisymmetric mesh
mesh_cell_count.T_good_source: SU2 V&V validation mesh MESH_validation.su2 has ~67k cells. A wall-resolved 2-D axisymmetric jet with shear-layer + near-axis refinement typically wants 30k-200k cells. Hand-set generously to allow OpenFOAM-style block meshes (often denser) and SU2-style unstructured meshes (often coarser).

final_residual_species.T_good_source: Hand-set; SU2 V&V config CONV_RESIDUAL_MINVAL = -14 (logRMS) is overkill; in practice a steady SST + species transport on this jet drops the species RMS residual past 1e-5 within a few thousand iterations.

centerline_velocity_at_xD_15.description: Streamwise velocity U on the symmetry axis at x/D=15 (m/s)
centerline_velocity_at_xD_15.T_good_source: Linear interpolation of Schefer paxv.jet.txt LDV centerline data: U(14.0)=46.568, U(15.1)=44.776 -> U(15.0)=44.939 m/s. T_good ~10% (4.5 m/s) accommodates well-known SST over-prediction of jet centerline velocity (RANS spread ~5-10% near x/D=15 in the SU2 V&V plots).

centerline_velocity_at_xD_30.description: Streamwise velocity U on the symmetry axis at x/D=30 (m/s)
centerline_velocity_at_xD_30.T_good_source: Linear interpolation of Schefer paxv.jet.txt: U(27.1)=29.222, U(30.8)=26.540 -> U(30.0)=27.120 m/s. Cross-check: p30v.jet.txt y/D=0 row gives U_axis=27.191 m/s. T_good ~11% (3 m/s) consistent with RANS-vs-LDV spread at far-field stations.

centerline_velocity_at_xD_50.description: Streamwise velocity U on the symmetry axis at x/D=50 (m/s)
centerline_velocity_at_xD_50.T_good_source: Linear interpolation of Schefer paxv.jet.txt: U(49.1)=19.804, U(50.6)=19.253 -> U(50.0)=19.473 m/s. Cross-check: p50v.jet.txt y/D=0 row gives U_axis=19.465 m/s. T_good ~13% (2.5 m/s) — at this far station the centerline approaches the coflow value 9.2 m/s and small absolute errors accumulate.

centerline_propane_mass_fraction_at_xD_1.description: Propane mass fraction Y_C3H8 on the symmetry axis at x/D=15
centerline_propane_mass_fraction_at_xD_1.T_good_source: Schefer paxray.txt (Rayleigh-scattering mixture fraction along axis): F_mean(x/D=15.03)=0.522. For a binary propane/air mixing flow with conserved scalar, F_mean equals Y_C3H8. T_good ~13% (0.07) reflects scatter between SST and the experimental mixture-fraction decay rate visible in the SU2 V&V plots at x/D=15.

centerline_propane_mass_fraction_at_xD_3.description: Propane mass fraction Y_C3H8 on the symmetry axis at x/D=30
centerline_propane_mass_fraction_at_xD_3.T_good_source: Schefer paxray.txt: F_mean(x/D=29.79)=0.239 -> Y_C3H8(x/D=30.0)=0.238 by linear interp to the next station (39.0, 0.185). T_good ~17% (0.04) — Y_C3H8 decay is set by turbulent Schmidt number and SST predictions typically run 10-20% high vs experiment at x/D=30.

jet_half_width_at_xD_30.description: Jet velocity half-width r/D at x/D=30: smallest positive r/D where U(r) = 0.5 * U_centerline at that station
jet_half_width_at_xD_30.T_good_source: Computed from Schefer p30v.jet.txt radial LDV profile: U_centerline=27.191, U_half=13.595; linear interp on the positive y/D side between (y/D=2.5, U=14.629) and (y/D=2.8, U=12.844) -> y/D=2.6737. T_good ~11% (0.30) absorbs RANS spreading-rate spread; SST is known to over-spread variable-density round jets by 10-15%.
